text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate (gateway 502/504) and streaming disconnects observed across prod clusters (region-us/west). Rolling graph spike at 1934567810. Auto-ticket created: INC-4219.

alex: paging @sara (oncall) — seeing a spike in gateway 502s and a correlated uptick in client streaming cancellations.

sara: on it. thanks for the ping. quick question — is this affecting all models or specific routes? any customer RPS patterns?

alex: quick summary: errors concentrated on /v1/stream and /v1/chat/stream routes. non-stream generation endpoints show smaller increase but under SLO. A subset of customers report truncated responses + 502 gateway.

oncall-bot: @sara you were paged at 1934567892. Active rotation: sara (primary), mike (secondary).

sara: I’m joining a call. starting with gateway logs and recent deploys. @julia any deploys in the last 30m?
julia: no deploys from infra in that window. I see autoscaler events earlier (scale up attempts) but no new images.

alex: copied tail of prod-gateway logs (redacted):
```
[prod-gateway-1] 2026-03-15T12:31:05Z upstream http2 error: writev failed: broken pipe
[prod-gateway-1] 2026-03-15T12:31:07Z stream: client cancelled while flushing chunked frame
[prod-gateway-1] 2026-03-15T12:31:07Z upstream returned 502 from inference-node-2
[prod-gateway-1] 2026-03-15T12:31:10Z latency p50=80ms p95=1.2s
```

mike: looks like client cancellations -> upstream resets -> gateway 502 loop. We saw similar when keepalive settings were too aggressive and file descriptor exhaustion followed. Any spikes in FD usage?

julia: checking node metrics: inference-node-2 shows FD growth, ephemeral sockets stuck in CLOSE_WAIT around the timeframe.

ops-bot: Metric snapshot: gateway_5xx_rate +420% vs baseline; tcp_close_wait_count +180% on inference-node-2; active_streams dropped by 30%.

sara: immediate mitigation proposals — pick 2 to apply quickly: 1) enable temporary routing fallback to model-variant with smaller KV cache (route traffic off inference-node-2), 2) increase gateway worker_count / conn backlog and tune proxy buffer settings, 3) enable short-lived rate-limited 429 for non-critical customers to reduce pressure. thoughts?

alex: prefer 1+2. we want to avoid shaping customer traffic if we can reroute. Also add short-term patch: set nginx "proxy_request_buffering off;" to avoid buffering issues with chunked responses.

mike: I can kick the reroute — updating LB weights for model-route -> shift 40% to inference-node-3/4. Command: `curl -XPOST https://control-plane/api/v1/routing -d '{"route":"/v1/stream","weight_updates":{"inference-node-2":-0.4,"inference-node-3":0.2,"inference-node-4":0.2}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN'`

julia: I’ll patch gateway config on prod-gateway pool (one-off) — setting proxy_request_buffering off + increase keepalive_requests to 1000 and proxy_http_version 1.1. Applying config to a single node for canary then rolling.

incident-bot: Running mitigation runbook: reroute initiated at 1934567920, gateway patch initiated at 1934567930.

alex: verifying: I see 40% of traffic diverted; new 5xx rate on inference-node-3/4 is low. On node-2 5xx remains high but trending down.

sara: can we also confirm client-side disconnect pattern? any specific SDK or client IP ranges?

julia: logs show majority of cancelations originate from long-lived connections proxied through cloudfront edge us-west-2 — not single customer. User-agent header: Redwood-SDK-js/1.4.2 in many samples.

mike: possible reproducer: run a local curl streaming request and hit ctrl-c; observed gateway logs show same broken pipe. Repro steps we used:
```
# quick repro (dev):
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/stream?model=x"
# after tokens stream, hit ctrl-c -> observe broken pipe on gateway logs
```

julia: sticking point — when client cancels while gateway is mid-chunk, upstream inference worker fails to reclaim KV cache slot quickly and FD remains open. That causes slow leak until node restarts or OS reclaims.

sara: next ops step: drain connections from inference-node-2 and force restart process to free FDs. julia, can you schedule a gradual drain and restart? mike, continue routing. alex monitor customer-facing errors.

julia: starting drain on inference-node-2 now (soft drain 30s), will escalate to hard restart if FDs not freed. Command: `kubectl drain inference-node-2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30` then `kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-worker -n prod --field-selector=spec.nodeName=inference-node-2`

op-bot: note: performing restarts will cause a short window of increased latency for in-flight streams. announce in #general if customer impact extends.

alex: quick customer-impact check: support flagged 3 enterprise customers with truncated responses; estimated 2.4% of streaming sessions impacted in the 5m window. No P0s yet, but keep monitoring for escalations.

sara: good. prioritize customer-visible mitigations first. If reroute + restart reduce errors to baseline, we will close as mitigated and create follow-up for root cause.

mike: reroute finished. traffic weight now: node-2 20%, node-3 40%, node-4 40%. Observability shows dropped stream count on node-2. 5xx p95 on gateway decreased from 6.1% to 1.1% over 3 minutes.

julia: restart complete on node-2. FD counts normalized. patch rolling OK.

alex: running a smoke test from multiple edges (curl & sdk): streaming responses now complete and chunk framing intact. sample client trace attached: `trace_id=tr-8f23ab`, no 502.

sara: monitoring for 15m. next steps: create RC (root cause) ticket to investigate why client cancels cause persistent FD leak — hypothesis: missing read close on streaming proxy + slow kernel TIME_WAIT reclamation. Also add improved metrics: track stream cancels, average FD per worker, and add alert when close_wait > threshold.

julia: will open follow-up: INFRA-8763 — implement better connection teardown and add a healthcheck to kill long-lived CLOSE_WAIT sockets after X seconds.

mike: also propose SDK change: client should send final zero-length chunk and close cleanly. I'll PR a note to SDK team.

incident-bot: Incident state changed to MONITORING at 1934568200 (post-mitigations). Current impact: reduced to 0.6% streaming sessions with errors.

alex: on-call handoff: @sara handing to @mike for the overnight watch. Please pick up any follow-ups and make sure postmortem timeline is drafted.

sara: handing off. key artifacts: LB reroute (control-plane change id cp-8921), gateway patch commit g-patch-442, restart logs attached. If errors creep back, revert routing to original and escalate to infra-rt.

mike: acknowledged — will watch for next 2 hours, then rotate to next oncall. I’ll start the post-incident doc and include reproducer steps.

julia: added postmortem stub: https://redwood.internal/pm/INFRA-8763.

alex: thanks all. great rapid coordination.

ops-bot: Final metrics snapshot at 1934568485: gateway_5xx_rate back to baseline +12%, streaming_truncation_rate down to 0.4%.

incident-bot: Incident INC-4219 marked MITIGATED (monitoring) at 1934568490.

mike: closing thread but leaving PM doc alive. If anything suspicious, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
